entries.title: Exactly-once, as it is
entries.description: Apache Kafka 4.4.0 taken apart, part 5: the transaction coordinator, TV2, control markers on disk, the last stable offset, epoch fencing, hanging transactions and KAFKA-20734, what exactly-once does not cover, and the collection's findings register.

entries.title: Producers and consumer groups
entries.description: Apache Kafka 4.4.0 taken apart, part 4: the producer's accumulator and Sender, linger and batch size, partitioners across clients, idempotence and where it runs out, consumer position and commits, classic and KIP-848 rebalances, static membership and share groups.

entries.title: What an ack promises: replication and the metadata quorum
entries.description: Apache Kafka 4.4.0 taken apart, part 3: the commit ladder, what an acks=all ack promises, the two ways out of the ISR, leader epochs and truncation, ELR and last-known-leader election, the KRaft metadata log, controller failover, and what quorum loss stops.

entries.title: One request, on the wire and through the broker
entries.description: Apache Kafka 4.4.0 taken apart, part 2: the broker's thread pools and request queue, the muted socket, a real Produce frame decoded byte by byte, purgatory and the timing wheel, quota throttling, generated protocol schemas, and ApiVersions negotiation.

entries.title: The log on disk
entries.description: Apache Kafka 4.4.0 taken apart, part 1: the partition directory, the record batch byte by byte, an append that does not sync, sparse offset and time indexes, record-time rolls and retention, compaction and tombstones, and log recovery under hand-injected damage.

entries.title: Building on three clouds, and the ecosystem
entries.description: Terraform v1.17.0 in its ecosystem and on three clouds: the BUSL licence and what stayed MPL, OpenTofu v1.13.2 measured (provider for_each and state encryption as one-way doors), Stacks and Policy as out-of-process plugins, a multicloud AWS/GCP/Azure project planned and tested with no credentials, write-only database passwords end to end, mock providers, local policy failing open, and the 101-item findings register. Part 4 of Terraform, taken apart.

entries.title: State, refactoring and the feature arc
entries.description: Terraform v1.17.0 taken apart, part 3: the v4 state file, lineage and serial, locks per backend and the S3 default with no lock, workspaces and terraform_remote_state, moved/removed/import blocks, and the 1.5 to 1.17 features from check and terraform test to ephemeral values, query, actions, deferral, Stacks and Policy.

entries.title: The engine and the providers
entries.description: Terraform v1.17.0's engine and provider protocol read from the source: the plan-graph transformer pipeline, the DAG walker and -parallelism, count/for_each expansion, the per-instance plan and -minimal-refresh, provider processes and the go-plugin handshake, tfplugin6 and cty msgpack on the wire, saved plan files and the apply re-plan. Part 2 of Terraform, taken apart.

entries.title: The language and the front end
entries.description: Terraform v1.17.0 taken apart, part 1: HCL's scanner and parser, schema-driven decoding, cty values with unknowns and marks, the block schemas, directory loading, the init graph and early evaluation, and provider installation with the lock file.

entries.title: Networks, I/O and the long run
entries.description: Docker Engine 29.9.2 taken apart, part 4: port publishing as DNAT plus docker-proxy, the iptables and nftables chains, the embedded DNS server at 127.0.0.11, the stdcopy frame and the log pipeline, stop, kill and restart policies, health, OOM, stats and events, the 2013-2026 history, and the full register of 100 findings.

entries.title: How BuildKit builds
entries.description: Docker Engine 29.9.2 and BuildKit v0.34.1 taken apart, part 3: docker build as buildx over gRPC, the Dockerfile frontend and # syntax=, LLB as a protobuf Merkle DAG reproduced from alpine's provenance, the solver's fast and slow cache keys, context transfer, RUN mounts and the runc executor, and exporters, cache export and attestations.

entries.title: Images, layers and the registry
entries.description: Docker Engine 29.9.2 taken apart, part 2: the OCI image as a tree of hashes, digest vs DiffID vs ChainID, tar layers and whiteouts, a measured Docker Hub pull, credentials, containerd's content store and snapshots, the two image stores, and a local registry's push path and GC.

entries.title: From docker run to a process
entries.description: Docker Engine 29.9.2 taken apart, part 1: the docker run call sequence, OCI spec generation, containerd and the runc-v2 shim, runc's nsexec stages and 40-byte bootstrap message, the create/start FIFO, and the exit path.

entries.title: Combining, keeping, and how it got here
entries.description: Git v2.55.0 taken apart, part 3: merge bases and generation numbers, merge-ort, rename detection, conflict styles and rerere, auto-maintenance and geometric repack, prune's grace period, the commit-graph and Bloom filters, history to Git 3.0, and a findings register with reproductions.

entries.title: Mutable state and the wire
entries.description: Git's mutable state and transport, read from the git 2.55 source: the index format and racy git, lock timeouts, refs and reftable, atomic-but-not-durable publishing, pkt-lines and protocol v2, fetch negotiation and the push quarantine. Part 2 of Git, taken apart.

entries.title: The commit and its objects
entries.description: Git v2.55.0 taken apart, part 1: one traced commit, loose object bytes and names, the object lookup chain, pack deltas, .idx fanout lookup, and reachability bitmaps, with measured numbers.

entries.title: The tree that configures the fleet
entries.description: Chromium's 1,211 builders, its commit queue and its release branches are all generated by lucicfg from 125 Starlark files in the tree.

entries.title: DEPS, gclient and what replaced goma
entries.description: Chromium declares 451 dependencies in one 5,188-line DEPS file. How gclient sync reads it, how rollers rewrite it, and how goma became Siso.

entries.title: Blink, taken apart
entries.description: A teardown of Blink at chromium/src@f288fed6: layering, threads, the scheduler, bytes to pixels, Oilpan, bindings, runtime flags, web tests.

entries.title: The Sea of Nodes, explained simply
entries.description: A plain-language explanation of the Sea of Nodes, the program representation behind V8's TurboFan compiler: what problem it solves, its three kinds of edges, why instructions float, how the graph becomes a program again, and why V8 eventually left it.

entries.title: One Graph, No Boxes
entries.description: A close reading of Click and Paleczny's 1995 paper A Simple Graph-Based Intermediate Representation — every idea redrawn and worked through: REGION nodes, PHI alignment, projections, memory as a value, the Petri-net execution model, the vtable-as-opcode implementation, and the experiment whose result surprised its authors. Then: how the same technique applies to any data.

entries.title: One repository, many agents
entries.description: How git worktrees work, read from the git 2.55 source: what is shared, what is private, the one-branch rule, prune, sparse checkout, partial clone, and measured costs for running many agents on one repo.

entries.title: Parsing bash, taken apart
entries.description: How GNU bash 5.3 parses: a lexer that reads parser state, aliases, here-docs, recursive $( ), the Bison grammar, expansion, and six other shell parsers.

entries.title: Next.js routing, taken apart
entries.description: A teardown of Next.js 16.4 folder routing: file grammar, build, request path, rendering, caching, client router and prefetch, with measured costs.

entries.title: Anatomy of GitHub CLI
entries.description: How gh works, what you can call, where its data lives, and which system owns the result: commands, YAML configuration, accounts, credentials, Git, REST, GraphQL, Projects, Actions, extensions, agents, and a durable adapter for a session operating system.

entries.title: What the Parser Hears
entries.description: A field guide to JSON, YAML and TOML as configuration formats: their specs, their pitfalls, what 34 real parsers actually hear for the same bytes, and a practice for choosing and guarding a config format.

entries.title: What Compression Keeps
entries.description: How compression works — entropy, modelling and coding, LZ dictionaries, the 2026 codecs, prediction, lossy coding, HTTP and security — and how it differs from compaction in storage engines, logs, garbage collectors, git and LLM agent context.

entries.title: What Each File Wants
entries.description: A measured field guide to compressing JSON, config files, logs, tabular data, images, audio and video in 2026: codecs, levels, dictionaries, columnar encodings and media codecs, and when not to compress.

entries.title: What is a TOML file?
entries.description: How a plain-text .toml file becomes structured data, and how a program turns that data into behavior: keys, tables, types, parsing, validation, overrides, version compatibility, and the configuration boundary for a session operating system.

entries.title: Codex JSON, field by field
entries.description: A recursive reference to .codex-global-state.json: every observed object shape becomes a folder, and every leaf gets a section. Covers field meanings, writes, project and thread links, cached schemas, and the boundary for a session operating system.

entries.title: Turborepo or Nx
entries.description: A sourced comparison of Turborepo and Nx as of October 2026: graph models, cache keys, remote caching, distributed CI, polyglot support, governance, agent features, pricing and supply-chain history, plus a benchmark of both on one synthetic workspace.

entries.title: Where the JSON Lives
entries.description: A field guide to relational and non-relational databases, best practices that survive production, and a measured recommendation for storing JSON continuously with free, open-source components.

entries.title: A Table With Two Columns
entries.description: How to build a registry of pages that renders documents dynamically from their shape — schema, resolver, registry, renderer — and how MagicPath fits, with pros and cons.

entries.title: The State Is Enough
entries.description: What a Markov process is, what the memoryless property buys you, and where computer science uses it: PageRank, MCMC, HMMs, MDPs, branch predictors, queueing, and modern sequence models.

entries.title: Nothing Runs While You're Gone
entries.description: How simple mobile games model their state — lazy timers, per-player documents, command sourcing, replays — and how the same structures produce the retention loop.

entries.title: Anatomy of a Codex session
entries.description: What a Codex session contains, how it runs, where it persists, and how to control it: threads, turns, items, projects, commands, permissions, forks, SDKs, and background execution. A versioned anatomy for designing an operating system that can route work into Space and other products.

entries.title: Anatomy of a Claude Code session
entries.description: A teardown of Claude Code 2.1.280 sessions: identity, boot, the turn loop, the on-disk layout, the transcript graph, all 120 CLI options, settings and environment, the ~/.claude.json state file, permissions, the stream-json control protocol, the Agent SDK, the other doors into a session, offloading work to apps, and what an OS should own.

entries.title: Liveblocks, read for XO Space
entries.description: A reading of the Liveblocks documentation with xo-space in hand: what it is, where it fits, whether it installs inside the container, and what it would take for agents to build and share a Space without a person watching.

entries.title: The Ten Hardest Open Problems in Mathematics
entries.description: A status report on the ten hardest open problems in mathematics — P vs NP, the Riemann hypothesis, Navier-Stokes, Yang-Mills, Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer, Hodge, Langlands, twin primes and Goldbach, abc, and Collatz — what each claims, what has actually been proved as of August 2026, where mathematics is genuinely NP-hard or undecidable, the four kinds of infinity and why the continuum hypothesis has no answer, and a dated forecast of which problems fall by 2050.

entries.title: XO Space: the architecture
entries.description: The implementation reference for xo-space: how to install and run it, and the xo-project folder contract — written section by section, code first.

entries.title: The anatomy of Space Walk
entries.description: An XO Research illustrated explainer on the architecture of Space Walk — the geometry, the rendering pipeline, and how it becomes an evidence layer for the quirq.

entries.title: Mixture of Kittens
entries.description: An XO Research illustrated explainer on Mixture-of-Kittens, Cursor's open-source MoE training megakernel for NVIDIA NVL72 racks.

entries.title: The J-Space: a construction manual
entries.description: An extremely detailed guide to the J-space — the verbalizable global workspace found in language models by Anthropic's Jacobian Lens — and a step-by-step construction manual: estimating the averaged Jacobian, composing the lens, sparse decomposition by gradient pursuit, reading, steering, ablating, patching, and validating.

entries.title: Anatomy of a Personal Memory Engine
entries.description: An XO Research teardown of iai-pme, a fully local personal memory engine: capture, storage, encryption, hyperdimensional substrate, community detection, recall, consolidation, and the evidence behind each claim.

entries.title: Anatomy of an Agent Control Plane
entries.description: An XO Research teardown of xo-space, the local control plane for AI coding agents: the capability loader, agents-as-data manifests, four runtimes with four transports, the SSE turn protocol, the session index that holds no messages, encrypted GitHub-backed backup, and the modularity invariant that holds it together.

entries.title: What Is a Unit of Work?
entries.description: An XO Research illustrated explainer on the unit of work and quirq, the proposed unit of verified work.

entries.title: quirq whitepaper · a unit of work for intelligence
entries.description: AI has an input meter: the token. quirq is the output meter: value budgeted by a human owner, minted by machine verification against captured world state, costed all-in, and read over time as a trajectory.
